facts.text: Greenhills was built by the U.S. government during the Great Depression as one of three New Deal greenbelt communities.
The village’s original townhomes were designed in the International style and still house many third‑ and fourth‑generation families.
In 2017, the Greenhills Historic District was declared a National Historic Landmark, covering about three‑quarters of the village.
Greenhills began as a federally managed “sundown town” that used restrictive covenants to keep minorities out of the community.
The village’s radial layout and community facilities were preserved when it transitioned to private ownership in the 1950s and incorporated in 1961.
The James Whallon House, now the village hall, is listed on the National Register of Historic Places and reflects Greenhills’ early architectural heritage.
